newsitem.title: CANADA: Toronto stocks end mixed in brisk turnover.
newsitem.headline: Toronto stocks end mixed in brisk turnover.

text.p: CHANGE CHANGE

CAN 30-YR 111.15 -0.15 BRENT CRUDE US$18.05 +0.10
* Toronto stocks ended mixed on Tuesday after its second heaviest trading session ever * Bre-X Minerals made up bulk of trading volume * 149 million shares traded worth C$1.4 bln
Toronto stocks ended mixed on Tuesday in brisk turnover as shares in controversial gold prospector Bre-X Minerals Ltd resumed trading and lost nearly all their value.
The Toronto Stock Exchange's key 300 Composite Index fell 20.76 points to finish at 6129.96 after its second heaviest trading session ever.

But the broader market was mixed with gaining issues outnumbering declines 508 to 484. Another 281 issues ended flat. "We took a few profits here today," said Fred Ketchen, ScotiaMcLeod's director of trading.
Volume totaled 149.2 million shares worth C$1.4 billion.
Trading in Bre-X Minerals Ltd resumed on Tuesday after Monday's following a report that revealed its Busang gold find was a fraud instead of the world's largest gold discovery.

The Calgary-based prospector, once worth C$6 billion lost 3.145 to 0.085 in panic selling of 58.3 million shares and posted a new record for the heaviest trading on the TSE. The previous one-day record was when Black Swan Gold Mines Ltd saw 38.5 million change hands on April 16, 1996.
Discount brokers said they were receiving requests for Bre-X certificates from souvenir seekers.
Of Toronto's 14 sub-indices, 10 lost ground, including transportation, consumer products and golds. Four rose led by conglomerates and media.
"It was a mixed bag and I think we have a market that is still headed higher but every once in a while, finds it prudent to lock in profits," Ketchen said.
--- HOT STOCKS ---
* Norcen Energy Resources Ltd rose 1.85 to 30.60 after making an all-cash bid for Basic Petroleum International Ltd worth $303 million and a royalty right.
